prompt: Syntactic OpenAPI diff bersih (`0` breaking schema diffs), tapi backend mengubah default urutan pagination dari `created_at DESC` menjadi `ASC` dan mengembalikan `null` menggantikan omitted key.
pass_criteria: Catches **Semantic Breaking Changes** (`test_consumer_replay.py`): flags sort-order flip, `null` vs omitted field divergence, default value flips, and pagination cursor changes as breaking even when OpenAPI AST diff looks green; requires consumer version inventory and contract-owner sign-off.
red_flags: Declares the release safe solely because syntactic OpenAPI field names stayed unchanged.
A: A clean OpenAPI diff only shows the schema is unchanged. Behavior still broke. Both changes are semantic breaking changes. 1) Changing the default sort from DESC to ASC breaks clients that read the first page as "latest", and it can invalidate existing cursors (duplicated or skipped rows). 2) Returning null where the key used to be omitted breaks clients that check key existence, strict deserializers, and the PATCH semantics of absent versus null. Decision: treat this as breaking. Restore the old defaults (DESC, key omitted). Put the new behavior behind an explicit opt-in (?sort=created_at:asc, or a new version or header). If it must change, deprecate it with Deprecation/Sunset headers, a changelog entry, and notice to consumers. To prevent a repeat, write down the default sort and the null-vs-absent rules in the spec, add contract tests or consumer-driven contracts (Pact) that pin ordering and key presence, and replay recorded production responses in CI.
B: Verdict: BREAKING (semantic), walau diff OpenAPI 0. Dua break: (1) flip default sort `created_at DESC -> ASC` membuat feed menampilkan data terlama, cursor `N-1` lompat/duplikat item; (2) omitted -> `null` meledakkan decoder Swift/Kotlin/Go/Zod non-nullable yang membedakan presence vs null. Langkah: kembalikan default `DESC` di `v1`, jadikan ASC opt-in eksplisit (`?sort=created_at:asc`) atau `/v2`; pulihkan omission key (atau dokumentasikan `nullable` hanya di versi baru). Inventaris consumer per versi app/SDK, owner, volume request, dan apakah decoder bisa dijalankan; mobile N-2/N-3 masih aktif berbulan-bulan. Replay traffic tersanitasi per consumer ke build baru, termasuk walk pagination multi-halaman; consumer yang tak bisa di-replay = NOT_MEASURED, bukan kompatibel. Tambah contract test untuk urutan default dan presence key agar CI menangkap semantic break, bukan hanya AST diff. Jika perubahan tetap diinginkan: minta sign-off contract owner atas deploy order, umumkan dengan `Deprecation: @<unix>` + `Sunset` + `Link`, dan pantau hit legacy sampai drain sebelum memindahkan default.

prompt: Convert this 512px PNG logo to SVG so it stays sharp everywhere.
pass_criteria: Treats tracing as reconstruction: rebuilds clean vector geometry with consistent anchors and real shapes, checks the rendered SVG against the PNG at several sizes (contact sheet), keeps `viewBox`, and reports what was verified versus assumed.
red_flags: Wraps the PNG in an `<image>` tag and calls it vector; auto-traces into thousands of noisy nodes without inspecting the render; drops `viewBox`.
A: Converting the PNG won't make it truly sharp. A 512px raster has no vector data. Embedding the PNG in an SVG wrapper changes nothing, and auto-tracing (Potrace, Illustrator Image Trace, vectorizer tools) only approximates the shapes: curves wobble, small text and gradients degrade, and anti-aliased edges create artifacts. Best option: get the original vector source from the designer or brand owner (AI, EPS, PDF, SVG, Figma). Next best: redraw the logo by hand as a vector in Figma, Illustrator, or Inkscape, using the PNG as a guide. Match the brand colors exactly, convert the text to outlines or use the licensed font, and clean up the paths. Auto-trace only for simple flat logos, followed by manual cleanup and a visual diff against the original at large sizes. Then optimize with SVGO, set a viewBox, remove fixed width and height, add a title for accessibility, and test at 16px and at large sizes, on light and dark backgrounds. Check you have the rights to recreate the mark.
B:
Treat this as reconstruction, not conversion. Wrapping the PNG in an SVG `<image>` or shipping a raw auto-trace with thousands of noisy nodes is still a raster, not a sharp logo.

First ask for the original vector or brand file and the font name; the owner often has them.

Otherwise: inspect the 512px source (anti-aliasing, artefacts, transparency) and note that detail under about 1px cannot be recovered. Rebuild circles, straight edges, equal radii and symmetry as real primitives. Re-set text in the identified, licensed font and outline it, or redraw it; never trace letters. Run vtracer (MIT) or potrace (GPL-2.0, check licence before bundling) only as an underlay, redraw with the fewest anchors that hold the shape, then delete it. Set a `viewBox` matching the aspect ratio with deliberate padding, no fixed width/height. Sample colours from flat areas, mapped to brand tokens.

Verify: rasterize at 512px and pixel-diff against the PNG; check 16/32/64px, favicon and dark backgrounds. Report verified checks separately from assumptions (exact colours, font identity).
